fields.acceptance: go test -trimpath -count=1 ./cmd/rhiza -run '^Test(NewCtx|Run|SelfPath|TUI)' passes, with a new test (TestRunConcurrentDirs) that calls run() from two goroutines on two scratch repos with different working directories and environments and shows each answers for its own repo; go test -race -trimpath -count=1 ./cmd/rhiza -run '^TestRunConcurrentDirs$' is clean; go vet ./cmd/rhiza is clean. Failure case: a working directory that does not exist still fails with the 'working directory' error. The binary's behaviour is unchanged: go test -trimpath ./cmd/rhiza -run 'TestScripts/(tui|daemon-self)' passes. Touches cmd/rhiza/main.go, ctx.go, tui.go and their tests. Must not change any command's output, flags or exit codes.
fields.statement: cmd/rhiza's run() depends on no process-wide state: it takes its working directory and its own binary's path as parameters instead of reading os.Getwd (ctx.go:42) and os.Args[0] (selfPath, ctx.go:421), tui.go opens a project's folder by passing it instead of os.Chdir, and nothing on the call path sets environment variables or package variables, so two run() calls can proceed at once in one process

fields.acceptance: go test -trimpath -count=1 ./cmd/rhiza passes, with every script under cmd/rhiza/testdata/script run; the scripts that still use the binary are named in one list in cmd/rhiza/main_test.go with the reason for each. Measure in the commit's Checks: block, on a quiet VM: /usr/bin/time -f '%e s %S sys' go test -trimpath -count=1 ./cmd/rhiza before and after, and the number of rhiza processes started (a counter the real-binary path increments) before and after (2026-11-15: about 5,330 rhiza lines). Failure case: a script whose fake bin/ command calls rhiza back and is left off the list fails with a message naming the list. AGENTS.md's Tests bullet ('They run in-process via testscript.Main') and agents/developing.md:21 are corrected to say what holds. Touches cmd/rhiza/main_test.go, the txtar files that need adjusting, AGENTS.md and agents/developing.md. Must not delete or skip a script (ls cmd/rhiza/testdata/script/*.txtar | wc -l is unchanged) or weaken a script's assertions.
fields.statement: cmd/rhiza's testscripts run each rhiza line in-process, as a script command that calls run() with the script's working directory, environment and standard streams, and only the scripts that need a process (a fake bin/ command that calls rhiza back, or rhiza run in the background with &) get a real rhiza binary, built once per test binary, on PATH; AGENTS.md's Tests section says which lines run in-process and which run the binary
